page: Amazon Web Services r7gd.large is an arm64-based memory-optimized instance managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs powered by the AWS Graviton3 Neoverse-V1 processor running at 2.6 GHz. Memory provision stands at 16.0 GB total, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance includes a 118 GB local NVMe SSD instance storage volume and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps, with zero GPUs.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate competitive single-core performance alongside lower aggregate throughput due to the small 2-core configuration. Geekbench single-core achieved 1475.0 points (average range), while the multi-core score fell to 2659.0 (weak range). In stress-ng evaluations, the single-core score of 1532.79 ranked average, whereas multi-core reached 3043.58 (weak range). Large-block read memory bandwidth was recorded at 53.54 GB/s, while write bandwidth measured 20.4 GB/s. Application tests reflect 3.46 million Redis SET operations per second and static web serving throughput of 4.26 GB/s.

The r7gd.large profile is cost-efficient for applications requiring high memory capacity and fast, ephemeral local storage without needing heavy multithreaded compute. The primary tradeoff is the 2-vCPU ceiling, which bounds parallel processing, software compilation, and LLM inference. Recommended workloads include in-memory caches, small relational databases, local buffer caching, and lightweight data staging pipelines.
